about.title: Imperial Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Imperial's economy runs on agriculture, transport, and small-scale industry, and workers here face real risks from heavy machinery, repetitive strain, and vehicle traffic on corridors like Rt 86, 2nd Street, and Clark Road. In most cases, an injured worker's path forward is a workers' compensation claim through their employer, since California law generally makes that the exclusive remedy regardless of fault. But if a third party contributed to the harm — a subcontractor on a job site, a negligent driver near Aten Road, or a defective piece of equipment — a separate injury claim may also be possible. Imperial County's smaller labor market and rural stretches don't change these legal protections, but they can make navigating two systems at once confusing. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge fees; we simply connect injured workers in Imperial with an independent attorney who can look at both the workers' comp side and any third-party liability. There's no cost to find out where you stand.

items.title: We Help Untangle Comp vs. Third-Party Claims
items.desc: California generally limits injured workers to workers' compensation against their employer, but a negligent third party can open a separate claim. An attorney can help sort out which path — or both — applies to your situation.

items.title: Timing Matters, Especially Early On
items.desc: Workplace injuries must typically be reported to an employer within 30 days, while a third-party claim carries its own two-year deadline. Missing either window can limit your options, so getting guidance early is worthwhile.

items.title: Retaliation Protection Is on Your Side
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from punishing workers for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about your job, an independent attorney can explain your rights before you take the next step.

items.question: I was hurt at a warehouse job near Aten Road. Do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is the required path against your employer, regardless of who was at fault. However, if equipment, a subcontractor, or another company contributed to the accident, a separate third-party claim may also be available. An independent attorney can review the details and tell you which options apply.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury to my employer in Imperial?
items.answer: California generally requires injured workers to notify their employer within 30 days of the incident. Waiting longer can complicate your workers' compensation claim, so it's best to report as soon as you're able. If a third party was also involved, that claim carries a separate two-year deadline.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workers' comp claim?
items.answer: No — California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an attorney can help you understand your rights and next steps. This protection applies regardless of the size of the employer or industry.
